review_candidates.title: Theoretical Physicist Research Assistant
review_candidates.description: ABOUT US ISFS SA is a research and development organisation that explores the connections between general relativity and quantum mechanics, and their potential applications in propulsion and quantum vacuum energy. Based in Martigny, Valais, ISFS SA conducts fundamental physics research, particularly on fundamental theoretical physics, alongside a team of about 25 people. The theoretical research builds on the theory of force unification developed by our team of physicists, aiming to connect general relativity and quantum mechanics within a unified framework. THE ROLE As part of the theoretical physics research team, you will contribute to the development, critical assessment and validation of theoretical frameworks in fundamental physics. Your work will combine analytical derivations, symbolic calculations and mathematical modelling, with particular attention to mathematical consistency, physical interpretation and testable predictions. You will contribute to developing and running numerical simulations, and to extending academic and commercial scientific software by implementing missing models, computational methods and software libraries. You will verify these implementations against established results and benchmark problems, documenting their assumptions, accuracy and limitations to support reproducible research. A central part of the role will involve confronting theoretical predictions with publicly available experimental and observational data from relevant physical measurements. You will identify suitable datasets, assess their quality and applicability, account for uncertainties, and determine where the results support, constrain or challenge the proposed models. You will work under the scientific supervision of the designated team leadership, including the company’s founder, in accordance with the established reporting structure and research priorities. Close collaboration with other team members is essential, alongside independent scientific judgement and constructive discussion of methods, assumptions and results. You will provide regular, rigorous progress reports documenting calculations, findings, difficulties and proposed next steps. Together with the team, you will define clear objectives, milestones, benchmark cases and validation criteria at each stage of the research. You will be encouraged to propose new research directions and methodological improvements, communicate findings in internal discussions and scientific presentations, and contribute to research papers for submission to peer-reviewed journals. WHAT YOU WILL GAIN You will join an international research environment, with opportunities to collaborate with experimental partners and research teams to assess the latest predictions of the theoretical frameworks under investigation. Working across different areas of theoretical physics, you will explore connections between disciplines and develop mathematical models and numerical methods. Close collaboration with the company’s experimental department will allow you to connect theoretical work with practical measurements and contribute to the design of experimental tests. You will benefit from scientific exchange and mentoring from senior researchers in a friendly, supportive environment that encourages curiosity, critical thinking and constructive discussion. You will have opportunities to explore new perspectives on fundamental physics. The role offers opportunities to broaden your expertise in theoretical and computational physics, strengthen your scientific software development skills, and gain experience in multidisciplinary research. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES •          Contribute to developing and critically assessing theoretical models and calculations spanning general relativity, high-energy physics and quantum many-body theory, investigating connections where physically and mathematically justified. •          Derive analytical results, examine underlying assumptions, and assess mathematical consistency, physical interpretation and testable predictions. •          Formalise selected mathematical results using the Lean 4 proof assistant and its Mathlib library. •          Develop, optimise and run parallel numerical simulations using Fortran, C++ and MPI on high-performance computing systems, with guidance from senior researchers. •          Perform symbolic and numerical calculations using Python (NumPy, SciPy, SymPy), Mathematica, MATLAB, CoCalc and other relevant scientific tools. •          Extend academic and commercial scientific software by implementing and validating additional models, algorithms and computational libraries. •          Verify computational implementations against analytical solutions, established results and benchmark problems; assess numerical convergence, stability and accuracy. •          Analyse publicly available experimental and observational datasets, quantify uncertainties, and compare theoretical predictions with relevant measurements. •          Collaborate closely with the experimental department and external research partners to identify measurable predictions and contribute to the design and interpretation of experimental tests. •          Use large language models (LLMs) as research tools in a rigorous and traceable manner, independently verifying their outputs. •          Maintain clear, reproducible documentation of derivations, assumptions, methods, code and results using LaTeX, version control and computational notebooks. •          Define research milestones, benchmarks and validation criteria with the scientific leadership; provide regular progress reports and propose improvements and new research directions. •          Contribute to manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed journals and prepare preprints, technical reports and supporting research materials. •          Present and discuss research findings within the team and at scientific seminars and conferences. YOUR PROFILE Essential requirements •          An MSc or PhD in theoretical or mathematical physics (recent graduates welcome). •          Solid grounding in at least one of the following areas: general relativity, quantum field theory/high-energy physics, or quantum many-body theory. •          A good command of core mathematical methods, including differential geometry, tensor calculus, linear algebra, group theory and differential equations. •          Scientific programming skills in Python, including NumPy, SciPy and SymPy. •          Familiarity with LaTeX and version control, or the willingness to learn them quickly. •          English proficiency at CEFR level C1 or above. Desirable qualifications •          Experience with Fortran and/or C++, MPI-based parallel computing or HPC environments. •          Experience in numerical analysis and validating computational methods against analytical results or benchmarks. •          Any peer-reviewed publication is a plus. •          Initial experience with Lean 4 and Mathlib, or interest in learning it. •          Thoughtful use of large language models for scientific work, with independent verification of their outputs. •          Experience extending scientific software with new models, algorithms or libraries. •          Experience with Mathematica, MATLAB, Maple or SageMath. •          Research experience connecting gravitation, quantum field theory or quantum many-body methods. •          Experience collaborating with experimental researchers. •          A good command of French and/or German. Personal qualities •          Capacity to learn an unfamiliar theoretical framework quickly, test it critically, and work productively within it without either uncritical acceptance or reflexive dismissal. •          Intellectual honesty: reporting clearly when a calculation fails or a result contradicts expectations. •          Comfort with open-ended, uncertain problems, and perseverance when progress is slow. •          Rigour and care in checking one's own work before sharing it, with clear documentation. •          Openness to feedback and a habit of asking questions early. •          Ability to collaborate closely and explain theoretical results to experimentalists and non-specialists. •          Scientific curiosity across disciplines, and the ability to work autonomously while staying aligned with team objectives. WHAT WE OFFER ·      A performance-related bonus. ·      Flexibility and autonomy in organising your work. ·      Career development opportunities. ·      Access to state-of-the-art computing and AI tools within a theoretical physics research team. HOW TO APPLY Please email your application to careers@spacefed.com , including: ·      Your CV in PDF format; ·      A list of your scientific publications, if any. ·      A link to your Master's or PhD thesis, or a PDF copy if it is not available online. ·      A brief cover letter outlining your research interests, relevant experience and motivation for joining the team. ·      Optionally, up to two representative publications or preprints highlighting your contributions.

B2) zvládáš bez problému.
